name: personal number (on the national card)
issuer: the Ministry of Interior's General Directorate of Nationality (civil register)
note: Landinfo's thematic note on Iraq's travel and identity documents (11 April 2018), read 2026-10-30, citing the Law on the National Card no. 3 of 2016 (art. 1(19), art. 34, arts. 27-28; an unofficial translation Landinfo holds, not public): with the new national ID card Iraqi citizens get their own personal number, usable in every setting; it is entered in the civil register and given to citizens when they apply for the new card; it has twelve digits and is printed on the card; newborns get their unique personal number (with the family number) when they are registered. Read as given on application (the card's), to citizens; a child born now is numbered at the registration of its birth, which the form's single `when` doesn't hold beside it. The Ministry of Interior's sites (nid-moi.gov.iq, moi.gov.iq) and the Supreme Judicial Council's legal database (iraqld.hjc.iq) answered 403 to plain requests 2026-10-30, and the law's own text wasn't found. The 2018 note is the latest read; the number's Arabic name isn't given there, so it is named as the note names it. No check digit, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: Landinfo (the Norwegian immigration authorities' country-information centre), Temanotat Irak: Reisedokumenter og andre ID-dokumenter, 11 April 2018
sources.said: Med innføringen av nytt nasjonalt ID-kort får irakiske borgere et eget personnummer som kan brukes i alle sammenhenger ... Nummeret blir registrert i folkeregisteret og gis til borgere i forbindelse med at de søker om det nye ID-kortet ... Personnummeret er tolvsifret og påføres det nasjonale ID-kortet ... Nyfødte barn får dette familienummeret når de registreres, i tillegg til sitt unike personnummer
